title: Riverton council votes to replace downtown garage with park
text: Riverton City Council voted 5-2 on Tuesday to demolish the 600-space Elm Street parking garage and replace it with a two-acre public park by 2028. The $14 million project will be paid for by a new downtown business levy and state green-space grants. Supporters say the park will draw foot traffic and cool the neighborhood during summer heat waves. Opponents, including several Main Street shop owners, warn that losing parking will drive customers to suburban malls. The council promised a free shuttle from an outer lot during construction. Public comment is open until October 31.
